work_orders.brief: Present the pulled sunflower anchor as a plant whose parts are about to be examined. Invite the learner to name one plant part they already recognize and note that there are parts both above and below the soil.
work_orders.evidence: The objective asks the learner to identify and locate roots, stem, and leaves, so the first contact must establish a need to attend to the anchor's parts rather than treating the plant as a whole object.

work_orders.brief: Recall that plants are living things and that they need water and light to grow. Ask which part the learner thinks reaches toward light and which part they think reaches water.
work_orders.evidence: The learner will soon assign each plant part a job, and prior-1 and prior-2 supply the only available prior ideas about plant life needs without introducing new terminology.

work_orders.brief: Using the pulled sunflower anchor, identify roots as the below-soil parts, stem as the upright part, and leaves as the flat green parts. State one role for each: roots take in water, the stem holds the plant up, and the leaves take in light.
work_orders.evidence: The objective requires locating roots, stem, and leaves on a labelled diagram, so the organise step must establish each part's exact position on the anchor before any practice occurs.

work_orders.brief: Reveal the spatial relationship among the three parts of the pulled sunflower: roots below the soil, stem rising upward from the roots, and leaves attached to the stem above the soil. The learner must see that roots and leaves are farthest apart and that the stem connects them.
work_orders.evidence: The slot is visual_required for a locating objective, and the relationship the learner must hold is spatial, so show-structure must make the relative positions of the three parts directly visible.

work_orders.brief: Test the belief that the flower is the main part that keeps the plant alive by asking whether a sunflower with no roots but with leaves and stem could still take in water. Use the anchor's visible roots to show that no leaves or stem reach the soil water.
work_orders.evidence: M1 denies the importance of roots, so it directly targets the lesson's required location knowledge: a learner who believes roots are unimportant will not value locating them correctly.

work_orders.brief: With the labelled sunflower still visible, have the learner point to and name the part that matches each given location cue: below the soil, standing upright, and flat and green above the soil.
work_orders.evidence: The objective is identification and location, so guided practice must keep the labels present while the learner makes the first location-to-name decisions.

work_orders.brief: Ask the learner to decide whether a plant whose leaves were removed could still take in water, using the labelled anchor to see that roots are the part below the soil. If the learner points to above-soil parts as water takers, guide them back to the roots.
work_orders.evidence: M2 implies leaves mainly shade and are not needed for growth, so this block tests whether the learner can hold the roots' job when the leaves are visually absent.

work_orders.brief: Check that the learner can identify roots, stem, and leaves by name and location in an unlabelled plant context, using the already-approved item selected for this check.
work_orders.evidence: The check must measure the exact objective — naming and locating the three parts — rather than recalling roles alone or reasoning about a different plant system.

document_title: The lesson opens on a familiar outdoor scene where one plant is visibly drooping and one is thriving, inviting the learner to wonder what an individual plant is made of and which parts matter for staying alive. Using a pulled sunflower anchor, the lesson locates and names roots, stem, and leaves, then confronts the beliefs that flowers matter more than roots and that leaves only provide shade. Practice first keeps the labelled structure present while the learner reasons, then removes it, and the lesson closes by checking whether the learner can identify and locate each part in an unlabelled context.
